previous_description: A named alerting rule that evaluates a condition against observed signals (metrics, traces, logs) on a schedule and fires a notification when the condition is met. Represents the alert definition in the monitoring backend (e.g., Prometheus alertmanager, Grafana alerting, Datadog monitors), not an individual alert event.
definition: A declarative rule configured in a monitoring backend that evaluates a threshold or query expression over telemetry (metrics, spans, logs) at a recurring interval and sends a notification to one or more destinations when the expression holds. It is the persisted rule definition, not a single firing or incident instance.

distinguish_from.when: the artifact only visualizes signals in panels and has no triggering condition or notification routing of its own
the symbol defines the measured quantity itself (a Counter, Histogram or Gauge created via a Meter) rather than a rule that evaluates that quantity
the thing is a single emitted event or log entry, including a record of an alert having fired, rather than the standing rule that decides when to fire
the severity threshold only filters which log records the SDK emits, rather than triggering a notification when a condition over signals is met

code_evidence: A Prometheus rules YAML file with a groups[].rules[] entry that has an 'alert:' name, an 'expr:' PromQL condition, an optional 'for:' duration and a 'labels.severity' value

An infrastructure-as-code resource such as Terraform 'datadog_monitor', 'grafana_rule_group', 'newrelic_alert_condition' or 'aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm' (or CloudFormation AWS::CloudWatch::Alarm) that declares a query or threshold and notification targets
An Alertmanager or Grafana contact-point/route configuration, or a monitor JSON export, that binds a named rule to Slack, PagerDuty or email receivers
notes: OpenTelemetry defines no alerting concept, so this type has no standard anchor. Missing attributes: pending/'for' duration, labels, runbookUrl and the hosting tool (dashboard has 'tool'). There is no SLO type even though the layer scope mentions SLOs, so burn-rate alerts lack a target. The 'dashboard monitors alert' relationship is semantically odd; 'displays' would fit better.
